annotations.description: Playing Hallowed Fountain before casting Thoughtseize is suboptimal sequencing. The player should cast Thoughtseize first (they already have black mana from Godless Shrine) to see the opponent's hand before committing to a land drop. Additionally, playing Flooded Strand instead of Hallowed Fountain would be better since the fetch land can be cracked later to enable Revolt for Fatal Push or to thin the deck, and avoids the 2-life payment decision. More importantly, with a 6/7 menace Psychic Frog and the opponent at 12 life with only 2 lands and no creatures, the priority should be casting Thoughtseize first to strip any potential answer (like a board wipe or removal spell) before combat, rather than playing a land that doesn't change available mana for the Thoughtseize.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Hallowed Fountain as the first action of the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Thoughtseize first using existing mana (Godless Shrine provides B) to see opponent's hand and strip their best answer before combat, then play the land drop afterward.

annotations.description: The player is being Thoughtseized (opponent's spell on the stack forcing them to discard a nonland card). They chose to discard Force of Negation, but their reasoning says they're discarding it to Psychic Frog's ability to grow it. However, this is a Thoughtseize - the opponent is choosing what to discard. Wait - the message says 'Select a card (discard cost)' which suggests this is actually the player choosing what to discard. Looking more carefully: Thoughtseize is on the stack, but the player is KimiK2 Vorthos selecting a card. Thoughtseize says 'Target player reveals their hand. You choose a nonland card from it.' So GPT5n Spike cast Thoughtseize targeting KimiK2 Vorthos, but the system is asking KimiK2 Vorthos to select - this seems like the target is choosing, which shouldn't happen with Thoughtseize. Actually, looking at the 'After' text: 'KimiK2 Vorthos discards Force of Negation (source: Psychic Frog)' - so this is actually a Psychic Frog activation happening while Thoughtseize is on the stack. The player is discarding to Psychic Frog to pump it in response to Thoughtseize. This is actually reasonable - pumping the Frog before Thoughtseize resolves. But by discarding Force of Negation to the Frog, they're giving up a powerful free counterspell. The Flooded Strand would be the better discard to Psychic Frog since it's a land and provides less value from hand. However, Psychic Frog's ability says 'Discard a card' - it doesn't restrict to nonland. Discarding Flooded Strand would also give a +1/+1 counter while preserving Force of Negation. Thoughtseize will then resolve and the opponent will choose from the remaining cards - but keeping Force of Negation would be much more valuable than keeping Flooded Strand.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Force of Negation to Psychic Frog's pump ability in response to Thoughtseize on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Flooded Strand to Psychic Frog instead, preserving Force of Negation which is far more valuable as a free counterspell. Thoughtseize would then likely take the remaining Force of Negation, but the player would still have gotten the same pump while keeping a land drop option if Thoughtseize had been countered or if the opponent took something else.

annotations.description: KimiK2 Vorthos resolved a Thoughtseize against GPT5n Spike and chose to discard Thoughtseize — a 1-mana sorcery that is far less threatening than the other options in the opponent's hand. The opponent has Teferi, Time Raveler (which shuts down instant-speed interaction and draws cards), Overlord of the Balemurk (a powerful 5/5 that mills and recurs creatures), Ephemerate (which can rebuy ETB effects repeatedly), and two Fatal Pushes that can kill Psychic Frog. Teferi is particularly devastating because it prevents KimiK2 from casting Force of Negation (their only card in hand besides a land) at instant speed, and its -3 can bounce Psychic Frog while drawing a card. Taking Thoughtseize over Teferi or Overlord of the Balemurk is a massive misplay.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to discard Thoughtseize from opponent's hand
annotations.betterLine: Should have taken Teferi, Time Raveler, which shuts down Force of Negation's alternate cost timing, bounces Psychic Frog, and generates card advantage. Alternatively, Overlord of the Balemurk would also have been a strong pick as a major threat.

annotations.description: Psychic Frog was already at sufficient power (6+) to deal lethal damage to the opponent at 6 life with no blockers. Discarding a card to pump it further wastes a card for pure overkill damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Psychic Frog's discard ability to pump it beyond lethal, unnecessarily spending a card.
annotations.betterLine: Simply pass without activating the ability - the Frog already deals lethal combat damage. Preserve the card in hand in case something unexpected happens or for future value.

annotations.description: Discarded Force of Negation to pump Psychic Frog when Flooded Strand (a land) was available as a discard. With the opponent at 6 life and potentially able to topdeck answers, Force of Negation provides crucial protection against noncreature spells that could swing the game. Both cards give the same +1/+1 counter when discarded.

annotations.betterLine: Discard Flooded Strand instead, preserving Force of Negation as protection against any noncreature spell the opponent might cast to stabilize
